A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same transformer-based in-context TD work. Their main texts, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original transformer-training experiments on randomized Boyan’s-chain tasks, architecture analyses, and numerical verification of its constructions in Section 4 and Appendices C–E.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds context-length evaluations, CartPole pretraining results, and RNN experiments in Figure 1 and Appendices F–G.

M1.justification: The transformer architectures, prompt constructions, multi-task TD algorithm, and constructions for TD(0), residual gradient, TD(λ), and average-reward TD are retained. CartPole applies the existing method; the RNN is an additional comparator.

E1.justification: v4 adds continuous-state CartPole policy-evaluation tasks with randomized dynamics, policies, rewards, and features (Appendix F). It also introduces the Loop evaluation environment used in the context-length studies. The earlier Boyan’s-chain coverage remains.

E2.justification: Appendix G adds a trained three-layer tanh RNN as an architectural comparator, contrasting its context-length behavior with the transformer in Figure 1. The existing batch-TD comparisons and transformer variants remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include MSVE-versus-context-length evaluation of a 15-layer transformer over 300 tasks and RNN evaluation over 500 instances per environment. CartPole pretraining uses context length 250 and 10,000 MRPs. These supplement the retained experimental settings rather than revise their reported performance under matched conditions.

E4.justification: Figure 1 adds a direct test of whether increasing context improves policy evaluation with fixed parameters. Appendix G adds RNN training diagnostics and context-length tests probing architectural dependence. The earlier depth, parameter-sharing, and nonlinear-attention analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Matched experiments retain 30-seed averages and standard errors, and CartPole follows that practice. New context-length plots also use standard errors; their 300- and 500-task sample sizes concern new evaluation designs, without changing replication counts or uncertainty procedures for retained experiments.

E6.justification: The original experimental plots are retained unchanged. New results show transformer MSVE decreasing with context (Figure 1), TD-like parameter patterns after CartPole pretraining (Figure 10), and reduced RNN training error without sustained improvement from longer context (Figures 11–12).

T1.justification: Appendix G.1 adds a derivation expressing linear-RNN predictions as linear combinations of input tokens and arguing that this prevents implementing TD under the specified representation, including with multiple linear layers. The original TD theorems, corollaries, assumptions, and proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The three central contributions remain transformer expressivity, learned TD emergence, and invariant-set analysis. v4 adds explicit priority claims for empirical in-context policy evaluation and theoretical analysis of reinforcement pretraining, while expressly disclaiming novelty of the pretraining procedure itself.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations connecting context-dependent improvement to learning rather than memorization, CartPole results to environment-independent theory, and RNN failures to architectural limitations. It also newly identifies practical restrictions from the assumptions and the need to generate tasks, especially for offline training.

D1.justification: v4 supplies an implementation repository URL where v3 only promised future release, although the old promise remains in the appendix. It adds CartPole parameter distributions, task-generation pseudocode, feature/reward processing, and RNN architecture and query-flag details. Existing optimizer, hardware, and runtime disclosures remain.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands and reorganizes the positioning around supervised versus reinforcement pretraining, interpretable network mechanisms, and RL training dynamics. New references include the Moeini et al. ICRL survey and TD convergence literature; earlier LLM-centered discussion and the Brooks et al. policy-iteration comparison are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around three explicit research questions. Related work moves from Section 6 to Section 2, the supervised-ICL background is removed, and empirical analysis now precedes theoretical analysis.

P2.justification: v4 adds the introductory context-length plot, CartPole illustration and parameter plots, and RNN diagnostic plots (Figures 1 and 9–12). Retained figures are redistributed within the ICLR layout, and the sequential-transformer comparison caption is corrected.

improvement.justification: CartPole validation broadens the previously Boyan’s-chain-focused empirical support, while context-length tests, clearer positioning, and added reproduction information improve the paper’s usefulness. The gains remain limited: the original training theory is unchanged, and Appendix G’s broad negative RNN conclusions exceed what its single small nonlinear configuration establishes.
